title: Calling
definition: Calling is God's summons through the Gospel by which sinners are invited and commanded to come to Christ.
summary: Calling highlights God's summons through the Gospel, by which sinners are invited and commanded to come to Christ.
christFocus: Jesus Christ calls the weary, the guilty, and the lost to come to Him for salvation and rest.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: In Scripture, calling is more than religious interest; it is God's gracious address to sinners through the message of Christ. The outward call announces repentance, faith, forgiveness, and the kingdom of God. The doctrine keeps evangelism urgent because people must hear the Gospel, and it keeps salvation humble because the invitation comes from God before it is answered by man.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Calling matters because no sinner invents the way back to God. The Lord speaks first, sends His Word, confronts spiritual death, and places Christ before the conscience. This guards the Church from treating salvation as mere advice, preference, or self-improvement.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Respond to God's call without delay, and speak the Gospel as a real summons rather than a vague encouragement. Ask whether your life treats Christ's invitation as weighty, merciful, and authoritative. Pray for boldness to call others to repent, believe, and come to Jesus.
